pairs.en: Abstract—Robust perception in snowy conditions remains a critical challenge for autonomous vehicles. To drive progress in this area, we introduce Snowy Scenes, the ﬁrst multimodal multitask dataset captured entirely in real-world snowy conditions, combining high-resolution 128-beam LiDAR data with synchronized RGB and thermal images. Snowy Scenes includes over 5 K expertly annotated LiDAR scans with 3D bounding boxes, per-point semantic labels, and snow particle annotations. This rich annotation set enables research on 3D object detection, semantic segmentation, and point cloud denoising, both as standalone tasks and within joint multitask learning frameworks. By benchmarking existing methods, our dataset paves the way for the next generation of perception models designed to handle the complexities of snowy winter weather. Index Terms—Autonomous systems, data collection, sensor fusion, object detection, semantic segmentation, signal denoising.

pairs.en: This letter introduces Snowy Scenes, the ﬁrst multimodal dataset collected in real-world snowy conditions using highresolution 128-beam LiDAR, RGB, and thermal cameras coupled with GNSS/IMU. Leveraging our 5 K rich annotated data, our extensive benchmarking experiments with state-of-the-art models show that voxel-based methods excel in semantic segmentation and noise removal tasks. Their capacity to capture ﬁne-grained information while being agnostic to LiDAR resolution makes them the optimal choice for off-the-shelf adaptation. When it comes to the object detection task, BEV-based methods outperform other approaches. Across all three benchmarking tasks, point-based models exhibit low performance due to their limited receptive ﬁelds. Additionally, our results reveal that unsupervised point cloud denoising methods are not resolution-agnostic and require further study. Additional experiment results are provided in the supplementary material available at https://github.com/snowyscenes/dataset. As future work, leveraging GNSS/IMU data in Snowy Scenes, we plan to conduct additional experiments to benchmark SLAM algorithms under snowy conditions and address potential challenges. Limitations: Snowy Scenes has no Radar sensor. The dataset contains only front-view limited RGB and thermal cameras. There is no annotation of RGB or thermal images. No other weather conditions, such as rain and fog, are included. Localizationand mapping-related benchmarks are excluded.
pairs.zh: 这封信介绍了Snowy Scenes，这是第一个使用高分辨率128光束激光雷达、RGB和热像仪结合GNSS/IMU在现实世界下雪条件下收集的多模态数据集。利用我们5 K丰富的注释数据，我们用最先进的模型进行的广泛基准测试实验表明，基于体素的方法在语义分割和噪声去除任务中表现出色。它们在捕获细粒度信息的同时与激光雷达分辨率无关的能力使它们成为现成适应的最佳选择。在目标检测任务方面，基于BEV的方法优于其他方法。在所有三个基准测试任务中，基于点的模型由于其有限的接收场而表现出低性能。 此外，我们的结果揭示了无监督点云去噪方法不是分辨率不可知的，需要进一步研究。额外的实验结果在https://github.com/snowyscenes/dataset提供的补充材料中提供。作为未来的工作，利用雪域场景中的GNSS/IMU数据，我们计划进行额外的实验，以在雪域条件下对SLAM算法进行基准测试，并解决潜在的挑战。限制：雪域场景没有雷达传感器。该数据集仅包含前视图有限的RGB和热像仪。没有RGB或热像仪的注释。不包括其他天气条件，例如雨和雾。本地化和地图相关的基准被排除在外。

pairs.en: Due to the nature of spinning LiDAR measurements, it is crucial to compensate for the distortion caused by motion during continuous measurements. The motion distortion is 10866 IEEE ROBOTICS AND AUTOMATION LETTERS, VOL. 11, NO. 9, SEPTEMBER 2026 Fig. 3. Route maps with sample RGB and thermal images, taken from ﬁve locations: a–e. The two Otaniemi routes align with each other, and the ﬁrst two images were taken at the same location at different times. The color of each image frame matches its corresponding routes on the map. The thicker colored parts of the routes indicate the annotated frames. compensated by utilizing a post-processed GNSS/IMU trajectory derived from Novatel Inertial Explorer software and data from nearby GNSS base stations. First, the LiDAR trajectory, deﬁned as the pose of the LiDAR with respect to time, is exported in the global frame. Second, to georeference LiDAR measurements point-wise into the global frame, each range and intensity measurement (i.e., point) is individually transformed into the global frame by using a pose of the LiDAR at the time of each measurement. The continuous LiDAR data is split into scans, i.e., full 360◦ rotations of the spinning LiDAR. To compensate for motion, the LiDAR readings from each scan are reprojected into a ﬁxed frame. The frame’s pose is deﬁned according to the LiDAR’s pose at the time of the ﬁrst scan measurement. Finally, the points associated with a scan are selected from the georeferenced point cloud and transformed into the ﬁxed frame separately for each scan in the LiDAR data to produce ﬁnal motion-compensated scans.

pairs.en: A. Vehicle and Sensor Setup As depicted in Fig. 2, our vehicle (Ford Mondeo, 2017) is equipped with a 360-degree, high-resolution 128-beam LiDAR, a front-facing RGB camera, and three thermal cameras. Additionally, the vehicle has a GNSS/IMU system for accurate ego-positioning. Detailed speciﬁcations for each sensor can be found in Table II. All sensors are time-synchronized using a GNSS/IMU sensor and calibrated as detailed in Section III-B. Fig. 2. Sensor setup for the data logging vehicle. TABLE II SENSOR SPECIFICATIONS OF SNOWY SCENES B. Sensor Calibration and Synchronization The global frame is an East-North-Up (ENU) frame deﬁned according to the ETRS-TM35FIN coordinate system. It is a Universal Transverse Mercator projection (ETRS89 / UTM zone 35 N) that spans the entire country of Finland. The up coordinate is deﬁned as the ellipsoidal height. The vehicle ego-frame and the LiDAR frame are the same. Its x-axis is positive to the right, the y-axis is positive forward, and the z-axis is positive upwards. The camera frame is located in the camera focal point (x-axis positive right, y-axis down, and z-axis forward), deﬁned with a 4 × 4 camera extrinsic matrix that maps data from this sensor to the LiDAR frame. The camera intrinsic matrix for the pinhole model is also provided, along with the Brown-Conrady distortion parameters, which account for lens distortion. All thermal cameras also have similar coordinate frames and parameter matrices that transform their data into the LiDAR frame, which is used as the ego-frame. The time synchronization of sensors is performed using the pulse per second (PPS) signal and NMEA serial messages sent by the Novatel GNSS/IMU to other sensors, which lock their internal clocks to the main time source. RGB and thermal cameras are hardware-triggered by the same Novatel GNSS/IMU sensor at 10 Hz. LiDAR data is logged continuously during data collection, and its measurements are later motion compensated (See Section III-C). For each motioncompensated LiDAR scan, the closest-in-time RGB and thermal images are associated with it. The data-collection frame rate is 10 Hz.
pairs.zh: A.车辆和传感器设置如图2所示，我们的车辆（福特蒙迪欧，2017年）配备了360度高分辨率128光束激光雷达、前置RGB摄像头和三个热像仪。此外，车辆还配备了GNSS/IMU系统，用于精确的自我意识定位。每个传感器的详细规格见表II。所有传感器都使用GNSS/IMU传感器进行时间同步，并按照第三节B中的详细说明进行校准。图2.数据记录车辆的传感器设置。表II雪景传感器规格B.传感器校准和同步全局框架是根据ETRS-TM35FIN坐标系定义的东北向上（ENU）框架。 它是一个横跨芬兰全国的通用横向墨卡托投影（ETRS89/UTM区域35 N）。向上坐标定义为椭球高度。车辆自我意识框架和激光雷达框架是相同的。它的x轴向右正，y轴向前正，z轴向上正。相机框架位于相机焦点（x轴向右正，y轴向下，z轴向前），由4×4相机外在矩阵定义，该矩阵将来自该传感器的数据映射到激光雷达框架。 还提供了针孔模型的相机内在矩阵，以及解释镜头畸变的布朗-康拉迪畸变参数。所有热像仪也有类似的坐标框架和参数矩阵，将其数据转换成激光雷达框架，激光雷达框架用作自我意识框架。传感器的时间同步是使用Novatel GNSS/IMU发送给其他传感器的每秒脉冲（PPS）信号和NMEA串行消息来执行的，这些传感器将其内部时钟锁定在主要时间源上。 RGB和热像仪由相同的Novatel GNSS/IMU传感器以10 Hz的频率硬件触发。LiDAR数据在数据采集过程中连续记录，其测量随后进行运动补偿（见第III-C节）。对于每次运动补偿LiDAR扫描，与之关联的是时间最近的RGB和热像仪。数据采集帧率为10 Hz。

pairs.en: Autonomous driving has undergone signiﬁcant advancements over the last decade [8], [9], [10], [11], [12], [13], [14], with notable benchmarks such as KITTI [8], nuScenes [10], and Waymo [11] providing large-scale multimodal datasets for urban driving scenarios. However, these datasets primarily capture clear weather conditions, limiting their applicability in winter weather. Table I provides an overview of the dataset landscape and compares our proposed Snowy Scenes with the existing body of work in the literature. In this table, we separated the datasets into two groups. The top half encompasses datasets that exclude snow, whereas the bottom half is composed of datasets that explicitly involve snow. It is, however, important to note that in some datasets in this bottom group, snow constitutes a negligible fraction of the whole set. For instance, snow covers only 2% of the entire dataset, i.e., about 2 K frames, in ZOD [4], and 12% (i.e., 800 frames) in Ithaca365 [5]. The snowy data rate goes up to 33.4% in SemanticSTF [3], corresponding to approximately 700 frames. Other datasets, including MSU-4S [2] and MAN TruckScenes [1], have more samples of snowy conditions, but they only provide 3D bounding boxes without semantic labels. In the case of Boreas [16], 3D bounding box annotations are obtained in sunny weather. Notably, CADC [6] and WADS [7] are the only datasets that focus exclusively on snowy winter conditions, making them the most similar to Snowy Scenes. CADC [6] is the ﬁrst to provide a fully snowy dataset for 3D object detection, while WADS [7] is the ﬁrst to provide 3D semantic segmentation as well as the labeling of individual snowﬂakes. Despite the substantial contributions of both datasets to the research on weather-resistant perception, they exhibit signiﬁcant shortcomings. CADC [6] suffers from 32-beam low-resolution point cloud data, and WADS [7] is a unimodal dataset. Furthermore, both datasets lack diversity in annotations. In contrast, as shown in Table I, our Snowy Scenes dataset has a diverse sensor suite, including 128-beam high-resolution LiDAR, RGB cameras, thermal imaging, and GNSS/IMU data. In contrast to all other datasets in Table I, Snowy Scenes takes a major leap forward with the most extensive set of annotations, including 3D object bounding boxes, per-point segmentation, and snowﬂake labeling across the entire 5 K point clouds. Note that a number of additional datasets are excluded from Table I, despite the presence of snowy conditions. This is because they either lack 3D annotations (e.g., MUSES [17]) or omit LiDAR as in BDD100K [18]. RADIATE [19] is also excluded because it provides only 2D bounding boxes on radar images without 3D annotations.

pairs.en: We introduce a new multimodal dataset, named Snowy Scenes, with over 22 K data collected using a highresolution LiDAR coupled with RGB and thermal cameras in snowy winter conditions only.  We provide a comprehensive human annotation of over 5 K sequential LiDAR scans, containing 221 K precise bounding boxes for object detection, per-point semantic segmentation, and labeling of falling snow particles. 60% of annotated Snow Scenes scans has active snowfall.  Leveraging Snowy Scenes, we benchmark various stateof-the-art models for individual and joint learning of three key perception tasks: 3D object detection, 3D semantic segmentation, and 3D point cloud denoising. These benchmarking efforts provide comprehensive baselines to support future research on multimodal sensor fusion and multitask learning in snowy weather. To the best of our knowledge, Snowy Scenes is the ﬁrst dataset that allows for the learning of multiple 3D perception tasks in a multimodal setup, logged under snowy winter conditions. A devkit with evaluation code and conﬁguration ﬁles to reproduce the experiment ﬁndings will be made publicly available with the dataset upon publication

pairs.en: Autonomous driving has undergone signiﬁcant advancements over the last decade [8], [9], [10], [11], [12], [13], [14], with notable benchmarks such as KITTI [8], nuScenes [10], and Waymo [11] providing large-scale multimodal datasets for urban driving scenarios. However, these datasets primarily capture clear weather conditions, limiting their applicability in winter weather. Table I provides an overview of the dataset landscape and compares our proposed Snowy Scenes with the existing body of work in the literature. In this table, we separated the datasets into two groups. The top half encompasses datasets that exclude snow, whereas the bottom half is composed of datasets that explicitly involve snow. It is, however, important to note that in some datasets in this bottom group, snow constitutes a negligible fraction of the whole set. For instance, snow covers only 2% of the entire dataset, i.e., about 2 K frames, in ZOD [4], and 12% (i.e., 800 frames) in Ithaca365 [5]. The snowy data rate goes up to 33.4% in SemanticSTF [3], corresponding to approximately 700 frames. Other datasets, including MSU-4S [2] and MAN TruckScenes [1], have more samples of snowy conditions, but they only provide 3D bounding boxes without semantic labels. In the case of Boreas [16], 3D bounding box annotations are obtained in sunny weather.

pairs.en: We introduce a new multimodal dataset, named Snowy Scenes, with over 22 K data collected using a highresolution LiDAR coupled with RGB and thermal cameras in snowy winter conditions only.  We provide a comprehensive human annotation of over 5 K sequential LiDAR scans, containing 221 K precise bounding boxes for object detection, per-point semantic segmentation, and labeling of falling snow particles. 60% of annotated Snow Scenes scans has active snowfall.  Leveraging Snowy Scenes, we benchmark various stateof-the-art models for individual and joint learning of three key perception tasks: 3D object detection, 3D semantic segmentation, and 3D point cloud denoising. These benchmarking efforts provide comprehensive baselines to support future research on multimodal sensor fusion and multitask learning in snowy weather. To the best of our knowledge, Snowy Scenes is the ﬁrst dataset that allows for the learning of multiple 3D perception tasks in a multimodal setup, logged under snowy winter conditions. A devkit with evaluation code and conﬁguration ﬁles to reproduce the experiment ﬁndings will be made publicly available with the dataset upon publication.
pairs.zh: 我们引入了一个新的多模态数据集，名为Snowy Scenes，其中包含22 K以上的数据，这些数据仅在下雪的冬季条件下使用高分辨率LiDAR与RGB和热像仪耦合收集。我们提供了超过5 K顺序LiDAR扫描的全面人类注释，包含221 K精确的边界框，用于目标检测、每点语义分割和降雪粒子的标记。60%的注释雪景扫描具有活动降雪。利用Snowy Scenes，我们对各种最先进的模型进行基准测试，用于单独和联合学习三个关键感知任务：3D目标检测、3D语义分割和3D点云去噪。 这些基准测试工作提供了全面的基线，以支持未来在下雪天气下多模态传感器融合和多任务学习的研究。据我们所知，雪景是第一个允许在多模态设置中学习多个3D感知任务的数据集，记录在下雪的冬季条件下。一个包含评估代码和配置文件的开发工具包将在发布后与数据集一起公开。

pairs.en: The dataset includes high-quality multimodal sensor readings captured by one 128-beam LiDAR, one 2.3 MP RGB camera, and three 0.3 MP thermal cameras, providing a benchmark for diverse perception models in snowy environments. Different from existing datasets, as illustrated in Fig. 1, Snowy Scenes provides not only ground truth 3D bounding boxes but also pointwise annotations of 27 semantic categories, including falling snowﬂakes, which is crucial to study the detection and removal of snow particles, a.k.a., point cloud denoising or desnowing.
pairs.zh: 该数据集包括由一台128光束激光雷达、一台2.3 MP RGB相机和三台0.3 MP热像仪捕获的高质量多模态传感器读数，为雪地环境中的各种感知模型提供了基准。与现有数据集不同，如图1所示，Snowy Scenes不仅提供了地面实况3D边界框，还提供了27个语义类别的逐点注释，包括飘落的雪花，这对于研究雪颗粒的检测和去除至关重要，也就是点云去噪或去噪。

pairs.en: Although there exists a substantial corpus of research [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6], [7] introducing various datasets featuring all-weather conditions (see Table I), these studies exhibit several deﬁciencies in multiple aspects. First, most of these datasets have a limited amount of annotated data dedicated to harsh weather conditions. For instance, snow covers only 2% of the entire ZOD [4] dataset and 12% of Ithaca365 [5]. Second, while certain datasets focus only on winter conditions, they evaluate only a single perception task, such as 3D object detection, as in the case of the CADC dataset [6], or 3D semantic segmentation, as in SemanticSTF [3]. Third, none of these datasets provides ground truth annotations to benchmark diverse multimodal 3D perception tasks in winter conditions. To address these limitations, we introduce Snowy Scenes, a multimodal autonomous driving dataset speciﬁcally designed to address multiple perception challenges posed by snowy winter conditions. Captured in the Otaniemi district of Espoo, Finland, during winter, the dataset comprises real-world urban driving scenarios featuring falling snowﬂakes, accumulated snow, and occluded road markings under both daytime and late-evening conditions.
pairs.zh: 尽管存在大量的研究语料库[1]、[2]、[3]、[4]、[5]、[6]、[7]引入了以全天候条件为特征的各种数据集（见表I），但这些研究在多个方面表现出几个定义。首先，这些数据集中的大多数都有有限数量的注释数据专用于恶劣的天气条件。例如，雪仅覆盖整个ZOD[4]数据集的2%和Ithaca365[5]的12%。其次，虽然某些数据集只关注冬季条件，但它们只评估单个感知任务，例如3D检测目标，如CADC数据集[6]的情况，或3D语义分割，如SemanticSTF[3]。 第三，这些数据集都没有提供地面实况注释来对冬季条件下的各种多模态3D感知任务进行基准测试。为了解决这些限制，我们引入了Snowy Scenes，这是一个多模态自动驾驶数据集，专门设计用于解决冬季下雪条件带来的多重感知挑战。该数据集在冬季拍摄于芬兰埃斯波的Otaniemi区，包括真实世界的城市驾驶场景，包括白天和深夜条件下的降雪、积雪和闭塞的道路标记。

pairs.en: Abstract—Robust perception in snowy conditions remains a critical challenge for autonomous vehicles. To drive progress in this area, we introduce Snowy Scenes, the ﬁrst multimodal multitask dataset captured entirely in real-world snowy conditions, combining high-resolution 128-beam LiDAR data with synchronized RGB and thermal images. Snowy Scenes includes over 5 K expertly annotated LiDAR scans with 3D bounding boxes, per-point semantic labels, and snow particle annotations. This rich annotation set enables research on 3D object detection, semantic segmentation, and point cloud denoising, both as standalone tasks and within joint multitask learning frameworks. By benchmarking existing methods, our dataset paves the way for the next generation of perception models designed to handle the complexities of snowy winter weather. Index Terms—Autonomous systems, data collection, sensor fusion, object detection, semantic segmentation, signal denoising.
pairs.zh: 摘要——雪地条件下的鲁棒感知仍然是自动驾驶汽车面临的关键挑战。为了推动这一领域的进展，我们引入了雪地场景，这是第一个完全在现实世界雪地条件下捕获的多模态多任务数据集，将高分辨率128波束激光雷达数据与同步RGB和热图像相结合。雪地场景包括超过5 K专业注释的激光雷达扫描，带有3D边界框、每点语义标签和雪粒子注释。这个丰富的注释集支持3D目标检测、语义分割和点云去噪的研究，既可以作为独立任务，也可以作为联合多任务学习框架。通过对现有方法进行基准测试，我们的数据集为旨在处理冬季下雪天气复杂性的下一代感知模型铺平了道路。 索引术语-自主系统，数据采集，传感器融合，目标检测，语义分割，信号去噪。
